claim_verdicts.evidence: Fowler, quoted in the guide: "There are objects, many named after the nouns in the domain space ... there is hardly any behavior on these objects, making them little more than bags of getters and setters." and "those data models will be used from a set of service objects ... which capture all the domain or business logic."
git show stage-1:DonHang.Domain/Entities.cs lines 25-35: Id, CustomerId, PlacedAt, Status (required), Items, Customer, each `{ get; set; }`; no method, no declared constructor.
Entities.cs lines 3-4: "// lesson: backend.l1.efcore-mapping" / "// One class per table in db/schema.sql. No behaviour here beyond what a row is."

Compiler half: round-1 run (net10.0, stage-1 Entities.cs + OrderExposed.cs) compiled `o.Status = "banana"` on a shipped Order, printed `banana cancelled`. DB half: db/schema.sql:22-23 `status text NOT NULL CHECK (status IN ('new', 'paid', 'shipped', 'cancelled'))`; schema.sql has no trigger/function, so the CHECK sees only the new value. Loaded as initdb (docker-compose.yml:67); MigrationBaseline.cs keeps Migrate() from recreating the tables.

"The `required` modifier indicates that the field or property it applies to must be initialized by an object initializer." and "You must initialize required members, but you can initialize them to `null`." Nothing restricts the value or later assignment through the public `set`.

OrderService.cs:10 `if (items.Count == 0) throw new ArgumentException("an order needs at least one item");` is the only check; :34 `order.Status = "cancelled";` unconditional (comment 25-28). git grep of Status/Count/Quantity in DonHang.*/*.cs (non-test): OrdersController.Create/Cancel only forward to OrderService; no [Range]/[Required] attributes; DbContext only maps column names.

Dtos.cs:3-4 "// The API answers in these shapes, never in the entity shapes from DonHang.Domain."; line 9 `public sealed record OrderDto(int Id, int CustomerId, string Status, DateTimeOffset PlacedAt, List<OrderItemDto> Items);` - positional record, no members with logic.

"a set of Domain Entities or Data Transfer Objects that can be used to communicate across application boundaries. These objects generally contain no functionality, or only minimal functionality"; anemic side: claim 1 evidence (named after domain nouns, logic in service objects).

"if your microservice or Bounded Context is very simple (a CRUD service), the anemic domain model in the form of entity objects with just data properties might be good enough"; "if you need to tackle ... a lot of ever-changing business rules, the anemic domain model might be an anti-pattern". Example now matches repo: price CHECK in db/schema.sql:7, no C# check on Product (see claim 12). Stated with a condition, not as fact.

OrderExposed.cs:4-11: "// Every field is public, so any code anywhere can put an order into a state" / "// the business does not allow: paid but empty, or with a negative total."; fields `public int Id; public string Status = "new"; public int TotalVnd; public List<OrderLineExposed> Lines = new();`

Executed `git grep -n "Status = \"" stage-1 -- "DonHang.*/*.cs"` in examples/don-hang: exactly three lines - DonHang.Domain/OrderService.cs:16 `Status = "new",`, OrderService.cs:34 `order.Status = "cancelled";`, DonHang.Tests/Services/OrderServiceTests.cs:49 seeded `Status = "new"`. samples/ excluded by the pathspec. Run with host git, not the 2.54 lab box.

Entities.cs:17-22: Product has Id, `required string Name`, PriceVnd, all `{ get; set; }`; no C# code checks the values (git grep PriceVnd: only DTO mapping). schema.sql:4-8: `price_vnd integer NOT NULL CHECK (price_vnd > 0)` but also `name text NOT NULL`, and `required` forces Name to be set at creation. "one rule" / "only rule" is slightly too strong.
claim_verdicts.suggested_text: At stage-1 Product has only Id, Name and PriceVnd with public setters, and no C# code checks their values; its one business rule, a price above zero, is a CHECK in db/schema.sql.

claim_verdicts.evidence: "Per DDD patterns, you should encapsulate domain behavior and rules within the entity class itself" and "Since EF Core 1.1, to satisfy those DDD requirements, you can have plain fields in your entities instead of public properties ... You can also use private property setters." - EF-mapped entities can hold rules; anemic = "lack behavior (methods)", logic in service objects.

issues.text: Product's "only rule" is a price above zero, but db/schema.sql:5-6 also has `name text NOT NULL`, and Entities.cs:20 marks Name `required`. Round-1 blocker is resolved (Product no longer called rule-free); this is residual over-precision. Same wording in claim 12.
issues.quote: as with `Product` at stage-1, whose only rule, a price above zero, the database checks
issues.fix: Replace "whose only rule" with "whose one business rule" in section 4, and "its one rule" with "its one business rule" in claim 12 (claim 12 suggested_text).
